$comment: Which conventions govern WHICH context — the join AGENTS.md and context-map.json never had.
THE GAP THIS CLOSES. AGENTS.md states repository-wide never/always rules and
context-map.json scopes files into 117 contexts across 16 groups, and nothing connected the
two. So an agent editing the LLM chokepoint and an agent editing a marketing page read the
same ~930 lines, and both pay for the whole surface before their first edit. The cost is not
the reading time, it is what the averaging does to the content: a rule that is load-bearing
in one directory and irrelevant in fifteen has to be written weakly enough to be true
everywhere, and the sharp local ones — the demo fallback is a product property, the store
has a sqlite twin, cs is the home market but en is the source — stay tacit, which means they
are learned from a red build or not at all.
WHAT THIS FILE IS, AND IS NOT. It is a ROUTING table, the same species as docs/task-index.md
and .github/adr-ownership.json: it does not restate a rule, it says which rules reach a
context and adds the LOCAL note that has no home in a global document. Two fields carry that
split, and the split is the whole design:
constraints  ids from .github/constraint-map.json. Global rules, already written down, with
a rung and a fence. Named here, never re-explained here — a second copy of a
rule is a second thing to keep true, and the copy is the one that goes stale.
local        what is true HERE and nowhere else, in the imperative, with the consequence.
Each entry carries `unfenced: true` when nothing would tell you that you got it
wrong — those are the lines worth the reading, and the reason this file is not
a summary of AGENTS.md.
WHY IT DOES NOT LIVE IN context-map.json. That file is REGENERATED by the Personas context
scan; anything written into it is overwritten on the next pass (the same hazard ADR-0012
draws around generated regions). It is keyed by `context` NAME rather than by path or by
uuid so that a rescan which moves files, renames a group or renumbers a uuid does not silently
detach a note from the code it is about — and a rescan that removes a context turns the unit
suite red instead, in test-unit/context-conventions.test.mjs.
WHY IT IS NOT COMPLETE, ON PURPOSE. 117 contexts do not have 117 surprising conventions;
most are governed entirely by the global rules and a row for them would be noise that makes
the sharp rows harder to find. `npm run context:conventions` prints the coverage census so
the omission is a number rather than an assumption. Adding a row is cheap and the bar is one
question: would an agent that had read AGENTS.md end to end still get this wrong?
HOW IT IS READ. `npm run context:conventions -- --path src/lib/llm/index.ts` answers the
question an agent actually has — what governs the file already open — and is the reason this
is a machine-readable file rather than seven more paragraphs in the canonical document.
HELD TRUE BY test-unit/context-conventions.test.mjs (blocking, inside `npm run test:unit` →
`check:ci` → .husky/pre-push): a context name the map no longer has, a `constraints` id the
constraint map does not define, a cited path that has moved, or a `local` note with no
consequence attached is a red build. A routing table that has stopped resolving is worse
than none, because it is read with confidence.

contexts.why: The one seam every AI feature in the product passes through, and the one where the global rules understate what is at stake locally.

local.note: The demo fallback is a PRODUCT property, not a dev convenience. With no provider configured every operation returns its deterministic `demo` answer, which is what makes the public demo, the e2e lane and every offline gate work. Making a missing provider throw is a one-line change that reads like error handling and takes the whole key-free surface with it.

The provider adapters are importable HERE and nowhere else. `adamant/seams-lib` fences them inside src/lib/ too, so a helper that looks generic and gets moved out of this directory takes its `@google/genai` import with it and goes red in a file nobody was thinking about.

A model constant added to models.ts must be pinned in test-llm/model-pins.json in the SAME diff, or accepted into its `excluded` list with a reason. The goldens, the bake and the budget all describe answers from a model none of them names, so an unpinned constant silently re-points the whole corpus.

contexts.why: The money seam. Everything here decides whether a request costs the operator anything, and two of its files are CODEOWNERS law files.

local.note: A route that reaches a model without going through `usage.consume()` AND the durable per-IP limit is a billing hole, and no lint rule draws that line — `sast` checks caller identity, not metering. Copy the guard chain from an existing paid route rather than assembling one.

The spend ceiling and the limit windows are anchors in scripts/mutation-catalogue.mjs with a pinned kill floor. Loosening an assertion in the tests that claim this seam does not go red here — it lowers a score in a weekly drill, which is the slowest possible way to find out.

contexts.why: The dual-store pattern is stated in one line of AGENTS.md's architecture list and is the single most common source of 'works offline, breaks in production' in this tree — and its reverse.

local.note: Every store here has TWO implementations behind one interface — Firestore in production, node:sqlite under LOCAL_DB — and a method added to one and not the other is invisible until somebody runs the half you did not touch. The 2026-07-16 sweep found roughly twelve modules that were Firestore-only.

The tenant key embeds the userId (`u_{userId}_proj_{projectId}`) so cross-user IDOR is impossible by construction. Build it with the helper, never by hand: a hand-assembled key is how that construction stops being a construction.

A local-schema change needs a numbered migration, not an edited SCHEMA constant. An edited constant applies to a fresh .data/ file and to nobody's existing one, so it works for whoever wrote it and for no one else.

contexts.why: The only context in this repository where a wrong change spends somebody else's advertising budget.

local.note: `SKLIK_WRITES_ENABLED` arms real mutations against a real ad account and is off unless the value is exactly `1`. Never set it, never widen the guard, never add a second guard modelled on it, and never run the write path against a real token to check something. This is RED under AGENTS.md § What you may do unattended: stop and ask the operator, every time.

The control plane decides which platform is the source of truth when several are connected. Changing precedence changes which numbers a customer's report shows without changing a single number in the store — a diff with no visible data change and a large visible consequence.

contexts.why: Routes nobody signs in to, on a schedule the repository declares and the platform fires — two halves that drift apart silently.

local.note: Every handler here authenticates through `src/lib/cron-auth.ts`, which compares in constant time. A handler that reads the header and compares it itself is both a timing leak and a `route-auth` finding — the fix is the shared helper, never a local comparison.

A seventh cron is a three-part diff: the route, the schedule in vercel.json, and the entry in .github/environments.json. Two of the three is a build that goes red at the manifest, which is the good outcome; the bad one is a schedule the platform fires into a route nobody declared.

contexts.why: Two settings here read like one, and collapsing them has a currency consequence.

local.note: Localisation is COLOCATED: a component owns its own `const T = { cs, en }` and consumes it through useT/getT. The central dictionary is for nav and footer chrome only. Moving strings into a central file is the intuitive refactor here and it is the wrong one — the type system is the parity check precisely because the columns sit next to each other.

`DEFAULT_LOCALE` (what an unidentified visitor gets: en) and the HOME MARKET locale (cs, which is what prices are quoted in) are deliberately separate and were split apart in 2026-08-05. Re-collapsing them prices CZK as USD, and nothing in the type system objects.

The authoring direction is en → cs, and it was flipped from cs → en on 2026-08-05. A `TODO: translate` on the cs side is a real gap; the same marker on the en side means somebody wrote in the wrong direction.

contexts.why: The foundation every styled component sits on, with two traps that are invisible in the file being edited.

local.note: Tokens carry a ROLE, not a colour, and dark mode is a token override. A component that reaches for a raw palette value is correct in exactly one theme, and the theme it is wrong in is the one nobody screenshots.

In Tailwind v4 an UNLAYERED rule beats anything in `@layer utilities`, so a plain CSS declaration silently outranks the utility a component is using to override it. That cascade is what produced the border-colour bug; put new rules in a layer.

The keyboard primitives here are what the accessibility budget's blocking rules assume — a widget that builds its own roving tab order instead of using them is the one that will strand a keyboard user, and the budget only measures five routes.
